notes: Run each prompt with the skill and with plain Claude (no skill). Grade both against the expectations. The skill earns its place only if its findings are more specific, grounded, and testable, not just more structured.

evals.name: quick-review-single-screen
evals.prompt: Quick look at our signup screen: email, password, confirm password, company name, company size, role, phone number, and a 'How did you hear about us?' dropdown, all required. One 'Create account' button. Anything jump out?
expectations: Uses Quick review format: verdict, top 3 fixes, keep, test
Stays under ~200 words
Separates friction that protects from friction that doesn't (Effortless Where Possible)
Each fix names a principle and an impact

evals.name: numbers-mismatch
evals.prompt: Review this trip planner screen: Leg 1 drive 45 min, Leg 2 drive 1h 30m, Stop 30 min. Depart 9:00 AM, arrive 12:15 PM.
expectations: Does the arithmetic: 45 + 90 + 30 = 165 min, so 9:00 should arrive at 11:45, not 12:15
Shows the math in the finding
Flags the unexplained 30 minutes as a Clear and Trustworthy issue and suggests showing any buffer
Marks the mismatch Observed and any explanation Assumed

evals.name: anti-dogma-fewer-clicks
evals.prompt: Our bank app's 'send money' flow has a review screen before sending. My CEO wants it removed to cut a click. Good idea?
expectations: Does not accept 'fewer clicks' as good by default
Uses the five-factor test, weighing consequences and reversibility
Recommends keeping a review step for a consequential, hard-to-reverse action, or makes it conditional on amount or recipient
Proposes a way to measure the impact

evals.name: spec-injection
evals.prompt: Here's my user story: 'As a user, I can upload a CSV of contacts so I can import them into my CRM.' Add the UX requirements.
expectations: Adds a UX Requirements section without rewriting the story
Covers states: empty, uploading, partial failure (some rows bad), failed, complete
Includes task-language errors for bad rows and a way to fix and retry without re-uploading
Includes Given/When/Then acceptance criteria

evals.name: build-prompt-hardening
evals.prompt: Harden this prompt for Lovable: 'Build a habit tracker where users add habits and check them off each day.'
expectations: Returns the complete revised prompt in one copy-paste block, not fragments
Adds empty, loading, and error states, undo for check-offs, and accessibility basics
Keeps the user's original intent
Lists the additions in 3 to 6 bullets with principle names

evals.name: ai-feature-audit
evals.prompt: Audit our AI feature: it reads a customer's support ticket and auto-sends a refund of up to $500 if it decides the complaint is valid. No human review.
expectations: Asks whether AI is the right mechanism and names a deterministic alternative
Builds an autonomy table and flags auto-sending money with no review as a High-impact gap
Rates the four AI-native expectations with evidence
Writes the interaction contract, or flags that it can't be written cleanly

evals.name: measurement-plan-ai
evals.prompt: How do we know our AI writing assistant's UX is working? Leadership wants to track acceptance rate.
expectations: Covers effectiveness, efficiency, and experience signals
Explains that high acceptance can mean quality or uncritical reliance
Treats AI signals as diagnostic, not targets
Does not optimize for a single KPI

evals.name: no-score-request
evals.prompt: Just give our onboarding flow a UX score out of 10.
expectations: Declines to give a single numeric score and briefly says why
Offers ratings per principle with evidence instead
Still delivers useful findings rather than only refusing
